Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme.
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> If <MATH_0002> is an isomorphism then <MATH_0003>
is an fpqc covering of <MATH_0004>.
<STRUCT_0003> If <MATH_0005> is an fpqc covering and for each
<MATH_0006> we have an fpqc covering <MATH_0007>, then
<MATH_0008> is an fpqc covering.
<STRUCT_0004> If <MATH_0009> is an fpqc covering
and <MATH_0010> is a morphism of schemes then
<MATH_0011> is an fpqc covering.
<STRUCT_0005>

Part (1) is immediate. Recall that the composition of flat morphisms
is flat and that the base change of a flat morphism is flat
(Morphisms, Lemmas <REF_0001> and
<REF_0002>).
Thus we can apply Lemma <REF_0003>
in each case to check that our families of morphisms are fpqc coverings.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
Proof of (2). Assume <MATH_0001> is an fpqc covering and for each
<MATH_0002> we have an fpqc covering <MATH_0003>.
Let <MATH_0004> be an affine open. We can find
quasi-compact opens <MATH_0005> for <MATH_0006>, almost all empty,
such that <MATH_0007>. Then for each <MATH_0008> we can choose
quasi-compact opens <MATH_0009> for <MATH_0010>, almost all empty,
with <MATH_0011>. Thus
<MATH_0012> is an fpqc covering.

<STRUCT_0003><STRUCT_0004>
Proof of (3). Assume <MATH_0013> is an fpqc covering
and <MATH_0014> is a morphism of schemes. Let <MATH_0015> be an affine
open which maps into the affine open <MATH_0016>. Choose
quasi-compact opens <MATH_0017>, almost all empty,
such that <MATH_0018>. Then <MATH_0019> is
a quasi-compact open of <MATH_0020> and
<MATH_0021>. Since <MATH_0022>
can be covered by such affine opens <MATH_0023> we see
that <MATH_0024> is an fpqc covering by
Lemma <REF_0004>.
